reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a scientifically debunked myth. Authoritative sources, including the MIT McGovern Institute, Scientific American, and Britannica, confirm that modern neuroimaging techniques (such as fMRI and PET scans) show nearly all areas of the brain are active at some point during the day, even during sleep. There is no large, dormant 90% of the brain that remains untapped; indeed, unused brain tissue typically atrophies, meaning any genuinely unused portion of the brain would degenerate.
